Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): the condition written on this row on 2-Oct-26 (it stays B only while the Banks row is Overweight) is no longer met, since Banks goes to Neutral on the credit tripwire; the Greek listings in the MI Pool are six banks plus Cenergy, HELLENiQ Energy and Motor Oil, with the live holding Ballys Intralot beside them, so the country letter was a second bank weight, and in a week when European sovereign stress is spreading from France to Italy and Spain a bank-heavy periphery listing is where contagion lands next, though Greek spreads themselves were not read. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case: Goldman Sachs's emerging market team (8 Oct) stays overweight Greece by name, Greece is not among the sovereigns named under stress, and the Greek energy names are on the right side of the regime; back to B if the Banks row returns to Overweight.
